title: Why Do Leaves Change Color in Autumn?
one_idea: Trees deliberately stop making green chlorophyll in autumn, revealing yellow-orange pigments that were always there and making red pigments from trapped sugars.

analogy.source_term: Trees stop making green chlorophyll in autumn, uncovering hidden pigments

analogy.limitation: Unlike a costume, the yellow and orange colors were inside the leaf all along — the tree just stops hiding them.

audience_misconception: Kids think autumn cold or frost directly causes color change, rather than the tree deliberately stopping chlorophyll production.

claims.claim: Trees stop making green chlorophyll in autumn, revealing yellow and orange pigments that were always present in the leaf.
Red and purple pigments are made by the leaf in autumn from sugars that become trapped as the leaf's connection to the tree closes.
Sunny days and cool nights produce the most vivid autumn colors.
The timing of autumn leaf color change varies by region and elevation, typically beginning in northern areas in September.
